title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Summary of the Symposium on Issues Concerning the Adjudication of Compulsory Liquidation Cases of Companies
keywords_en: On the adjudication of compulsory liquidation cases of companies
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Summary of the Symposium on Hearing Company Compulsory Liquidation Cases

Fa Fa [2009] No. 52

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Summary of the Symposium on Hearing Company Compulsory Liquidation Cases of the Supreme People's Court is hereby issued to you for compliance and implementation in light of the actual trial work.

November 4, 2009

Summary of the Symposium on Hearing Company Compulsory Liquidation Cases

At present, affected by the international financial crisis and the global economic recession, the number of company compulsory liquidation cases arising from operational difficulties has increased significantly. The Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II) (hereinafter referred to as Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law) have made provisions on relevant issues in the hearing of company compulsory liquidation cases. However, in view of the non-contentious procedural characteristics of such cases and the current imperfections in the norms for liquidation procedures, it is necessary to further clarify the principles for hearing such cases, refine relevant procedural and substantive provisions, better regulate the market exit of companies, maintain the order of market operations, lawfully and properly hear company compulsory liquidation cases, and maintain and promote economic and social harmony and stability. To this end, after extensive research, the Supreme People's Court held a symposium on hearing company compulsory liquidation cases in Shaoxing City, Zhejiang Province on September 15-16, 2009, with the participation of some courts nationwide. Through serious discussion, the attending participants reached a consensus on the main issues involved in hearing company compulsory liquidation cases. This summary is hereby recorded as follows:

I. Principles to be Followed in Hearing Company Compulsory Liquidation Cases

1. The symposium considered that, as the main type of modern enterprise, when participating in market competition, companies must strictly comply with not only market access rules but also market exit rules. Company compulsory liquidation, as one of the important avenues for a company to exit the market, is an important part of the company legal system. When hearing such cases, people's courts should adhere to the following principles:

First, adhere to the principle of fairness in liquidation procedures. The purpose of company compulsory liquidation is to orderly terminate various commercial relationships during the company's existence, reasonably adjust the interests of numerous legal subjects, and maintain normal economic order. People's courts hearing company compulsory liquidation cases shall proceed strictly in accordance with statutory procedures and insist on achieving fair liquidation results on the basis of procedural justice.

Second, adhere to the principle of liquidation efficiency. Improving the overall efficiency of the social economy is one of the goals pursued by the company compulsory liquidation system. It is necessary to strictly but promptly cause companies that have already encountered grounds for dissolution to exit the market, minimizing the losses that may be caused to various interested parties. When hearing compulsory liquidation cases, people's courts shall complete the liquidation timely and effectively in strict accordance with legal provisions, ensure that the interests of creditors, shareholders, and other interested parties are realized in a timely manner, avoid unnecessary losses to relevant interested parties due to prolonged delays in liquidation, and ensure the effective use of social resources.

Third, adhere to the principle of balanced protection of interests. In company compulsory liquidation, the principle of maintaining a balance of interests of all parties in the company shall be upheld to achieve fairness and justice in the company's exit stage. When hearing company compulsory liquidation cases, people's courts shall fully protect the interests of creditors, while also taking into account the interests of employees, shareholders, and society, properly handle conflicts of interest among all parties, and achieve an organic unity of legal and social effects.

II. Jurisdiction over Compulsory Liquidation Cases

2. Jurisdiction over company compulsory liquidation cases shall be determined separately from the perspectives of territorial jurisdiction and hierarchical jurisdiction. The court with territorial jurisdiction shall be the people's court at the company's domicile, i.e., the court at the location of the company's principal place of business; if the location of the company's principal place of business is unclear or disputed, jurisdiction shall be with the people's court at the place of the company's registration. Hierarchical jurisdiction shall be determined according to the level of the company registration authority. Specifically, the basic people's court shall have jurisdiction over company compulsory liquidation cases of companies approved and registered by the company registration authority at the county, county-level city, or district level; the intermediate people's court shall have jurisdiction over company compulsory liquidation cases of companies approved and registered by the company registration authority at the prefecture, prefecture-level city, or higher level. If there are special reasons, the provisions of Article 4 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 37 and 39 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China may also be applied mutatis mutandis to determine the trial court for company compulsory liquidation cases.

III. Case Number Management for Compulsory Liquidation Cases

3. After receiving an application from an applicant for compulsory liquidation of a company, the case-filing division of the people's court shall promptly file the case with the number "(   ) Fa X Qing (Yu) Zi No. X". After filing the case, the case-filing division shall transfer the application and other relevant materials submitted by the applicant to the trial division hearing compulsory liquidation cases for review, and the trial division shall render a ruling on whether to accept the compulsory liquidation application in accordance with the law.

4. If the trial division rules not to accept the compulsory liquidation application, after the ruling takes effect, the company compulsory liquidation case shall be closed with the number "(   ) Fa X Qing (Yu) Zi No. X". If the trial division rules to accept the compulsory liquidation application, the case-filing division shall file the case with the number "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X".

5. After the trial division rules to accept the compulsory liquidation application, civil rulings, decisions, and other documents made during the hearing of the compulsory liquidation case shall be numbered sequentially after the number "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X", for example, "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X-1 Civil Ruling", "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X-2 Civil Ruling", etc., or "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X-1 Decision", "(   ) Fa X Qing (Suan) Zi No. X-2 Decision", etc.

IV. Trial Organization for Compulsory Liquidation Cases

6. Since company compulsory liquidation cases are similar in nature to enterprise bankruptcy cases, compulsory liquidation cases shall be heard by the trial division responsible for hearing enterprise bankruptcy cases. People's courts with the necessary conditions may have a specialized trial division or designate a specialized collegiate panel to hear company compulsory liquidation cases and enterprise bankruptcy cases. Company compulsory liquidation cases shall be heard by a collegiate panel.

V. Application for Compulsory Liquidation

7. A company creditor or shareholder applying to a people's court for compulsory liquidation shall submit a liquidation application. The application shall state the basic information of the applicant and the respondent, and the facts and grounds for the application. At the same time, the applicant shall submit to the people's court evidence that the respondent has already encountered grounds for dissolution and that the applicant holds a creditor's right or equity interest against the respondent. If, after the company's dissolution, a liquidation group has been established voluntarily to conduct liquidation, but the creditor or shareholder applies to the people's court for compulsory liquidation on the grounds that the company intentionally delays liquidation or there are other illegal liquidation acts that may seriously damage the interests of the creditor or shareholder, the applicant shall also submit to the people's court corresponding evidence materials showing that the company intentionally delays liquidation or has other illegal liquidation acts that may seriously damage its interests.

8. If the materials submitted by the applicant need correction or supplementation, the people's court shall order the applicant to make corrections or supplements within seven days. If the applicant is unable to make corrections or supplements on time due to objective reasons, it shall provide a written explanation to the people's court and submit an application for extension, and the people's court shall decide whether to extend the time limit.

VI. Review of Applications for Compulsory Liquidation

9. When the trial division hearing compulsory liquidation cases reviews and decides whether to accept the compulsory liquidation application, a hearing shall generally be held. For cases with clear facts, unambiguous legal relationships, and sufficient and reliable evidence, after notifying the respondent in writing, if the respondent has no objection to the written review method, the court may also decide not to hold a hearing and conduct the review by written means.

10. If the people's court decides to hold a hearing, it shall notify the applicant and the respondent five days before the hearing and serve the relevant application materials. If interested parties such as company shareholders or actual controllers apply to participate in the hearing, the people's court shall permit it. During the hearing, the people's court shall organize the relevant interested parties to hear matters such as whether the applicant has the qualification to apply, whether the respondent has encountered grounds for dissolution, and whether the compulsory liquidation application complies with legal provisions. If another hearing needs to be held due to reasons such as supplementary evidence, it shall be conducted within ten days after the expiration of the supplementary period.

11. If the people's court decides not to hold a hearing, it shall promptly notify the applicant and the respondent, serve the relevant application materials to the respondent, and at the same time inform the respondent that if it has objections to the applicant's application, it shall submit a written objection to the people's court within seven days from the date of receiving the notice from the people's court.

VII. Acceptance of Applications for Compulsory Liquidation

12. The people's court shall, within ten days from the date of the hearing or from the expiration of the objection period, render a ruling on whether to accept the compulsory liquidation application in accordance with the law.

13. If the respondent raises an objection as to whether the applicant holds a creditor's right or equity interest against it, or whether the respondent has encountered grounds for dissolution, the people's court shall not accept the compulsory liquidation application submitted by the applicant. The applicant may separately file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration to confirm the relevant dispute, and then submit a new compulsory liquidation application to the people's court. However, this does not apply if there is an effective legal instrument confirming the above objection matters, or if there is clear and sufficient evidence of dissolution grounds such as revocation of the enterprise legal person business license, order for closure, or dissolution.

14. After the applicant provides corresponding evidence materials showing that the respondent has intentionally delayed liquidation in its voluntary liquidation or has other illegal liquidation acts that may seriously damage the interests of creditors or shareholders, if the respondent fails to provide contrary evidence, the people's court shall accept the compulsory liquidation application submitted by the applicant. If a creditor applies for compulsory liquidation, and the respondent's main assets, account books, important documents, etc., are lost, or the respondent's personnel are missing, making liquidation impossible, the people's court shall not refuse acceptance on this ground.

15. After accepting an application for compulsory liquidation, if upon review the people's court finds that the compulsory liquidation application does not comply with legal provisions, it may rule to reject the compulsory liquidation application.

16. If the people's court rules not to accept the application or to reject the application, and the applicant is dissatisfied, it may appeal to the next higher people's court.

VIII. Withdrawal of Applications for Compulsory Liquidation

17. Before the people's court rules to accept the company compulsory liquidation application, if the applicant requests to withdraw its application, the people's court shall permit it.

18. If a company voluntarily dissolves due to the expiration of the term of operation specified in the company's articles of association or the occurrence of other grounds for dissolution specified in the articles of association, or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders for voluntary dissolution, after the people's court accepts the compulsory liquidation application but before the liquidation group distributes remaining assets to shareholders, if the applicant requests to withdraw the compulsory liquidation application on the grounds that the company has amended its articles of association or the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders has resolved to continue the company's existence, the people's court shall permit it.

19. If a company is dissolved due to revocation of its business license, order for closure, or dissolution, or is ordered to be dissolved by a people's court judgment, after the people's court accepts the compulsory liquidation application but before the liquidation group distributes remaining assets to shareholders, if the applicant applies to the people's court to withdraw the compulsory liquidation application, the people's court shall not permit it. However, this does not apply if the applicant has evidence that the relevant administrative decision has been revoked, or that the parties have reached a settlement agreement for the company to continue after the people's court rendered a judgment for dissolution of the company.

IX. Application Fees for Compulsory Liquidation Cases

20. With reference to the relevant provisions on application fees for enterprise bankruptcy cases in Articles 10, 14, 20, and 42 of the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Fees, the application fee for a company compulsory liquidation case shall be calculated on the basis of the total amount of compulsory liquidation assets, at 50% of the standard for acceptance fees for property cases, and shall be paid in priority from the respondent's assets after the people's court accepts the compulsory liquidation application. If the assets are insufficient to pay all debts and the compulsory liquidation procedure is lawfully transferred to bankruptcy liquidation procedures, no additional bankruptcy case application fee shall be charged; if the compulsory liquidation case application fee calculated according to the above standard exceeds RMB 300,000, the excess portion shall not be charged, and any amount already collected shall be refunded.

21. Before the people's court rules to accept the compulsory liquidation application, if the applicant requests to withdraw the application and the people's court permits it, the application fee for the compulsory liquidation case shall no longer be allocated from the respondent's assets; after the people's court accepts the compulsory liquidation application, if the applicant requests to withdraw the application and the people's court permits it, the compulsory liquidation case application fee that has been paid in priority from the respondent's assets shall not be refunded.

X. Designation of the Liquidation Group for Compulsory Liquidation

22. After accepting a compulsory liquidation case, the people's court shall promptly designate members of the liquidation group. If the company's shareholders, directors, supervisors, or senior management are able and willing to participate in the liquidation, the people's court may give priority to designating the above persons to form the liquidation group; if the above persons are unable or unwilling to conduct the liquidation, or if conducting the liquidation by them is not conducive to the lawful conduct of the liquidation, the people's court may designate intermediaries or individuals from the "Directory of Intermediary Institutions of the People's Court" or the "Directory of Individual Administrators of the People's Court" to form the liquidation group; the people's court may also, based on actual needs, designate the company's shareholders, directors, supervisors, or senior management together with intermediaries or individuals from the directory to jointly form the liquidation group. If the people's court designates intermediaries or individuals from the directory to form the liquidation group or to serve as members of the liquidation group, it shall apply mutatis mutandis the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Designating Administrators in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases.

23. The number of members of the liquidation group in compulsory liquidation shall be an odd number. When designating members of the liquidation group, the people's court shall also designate the head of the liquidation group based on the recommendation of the liquidation group or ex officio. The head of the liquidation group shall exercise the powers of the company's litigation representative during liquidation. If members of the liquidation group fail to perform their duties in accordance with the law, the people's court shall, upon the application of an interested party or ex officio, replace them promptly.

XI. Remuneration for Members of the Liquidation Group in Compulsory Liquidation

24. If shareholders, actual controllers, or directors of a joint stock limited company serve as members of the liquidation group, no remuneration shall be paid. If directors, supervisors, or senior management of a limited liability company, or supervisors or senior management of a joint stock limited company, other than the persons mentioned above, serve as members of the liquidation group, remuneration may be paid at the standard of their average salary from the preceding year.

25. If intermediaries or individuals serve as members of the liquidation group, their remuneration shall be determined by negotiation between the intermediaries or individuals and the company; if negotiation fails, it shall be determined by the people's court with reference to the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Determining Remuneration for Administrators in Enterprise Bankruptcy Cases.

XII. Decision-Making Mechanism of the Liquidation Group in Compulsory Liquidation

26. If disputes arise within the liquidation group during company compulsory liquidation regarding liquidation matters, the matter shall be resolved by a majority vote of more than half of all members of the liquidation group, with reference to the provisions of Article 112 of the Company Law. Members of the liquidation group who have a direct interest in the disputed matter may express their opinions but shall not vote; if a majority opinion cannot be formed due to abstention by the interested party, the liquidation group may request the people's court to make a decision. If a decision is made by a vote in which a member of the liquidation group with a direct interest in the disputed matter did not abstain, creditors or other members of the liquidation group may, with reference to Article 22 of the Company Law, request the people's court to revoke the decision within 60 days from the date of the decision.

XIII. Preservation of Assets in Compulsory Liquidation

27. After accepting an application for compulsory liquidation, if the company's assets may be concealed, transferred, damaged, etc., which may affect the lawful liquidation, the people's court may, upon the application of the liquidation group or the applicant, take corresponding preservation measures with respect to the company's assets.

XIV. Hearing of Cases Where Liquidation Is Impossible

28. For compulsory liquidation cases where the respondent's main assets, account books, important documents, etc., are lost, or the respondent's personnel are missing, after providing explanations or imposing civil sanctions such as fines on the respondent's shareholders, directors, and other directly responsible persons, if liquidation or full liquidation remains impossible, but there are still some assets and partial repayment can be made based on existing account books and important documents, the people's court shall, with reference to the provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, conduct a fair repayment of the existing assets and then terminate the compulsory liquidation procedure on the ground that full liquidation is impossible; if there are no assets, account books, or important documents, and the respondent's personnel are missing, the compulsory liquidation procedure shall be terminated on the ground that liquidation is impossible.

29. If a creditor applies for compulsory liquidation and the people's court rules to terminate the compulsory liquidation procedure on the ground that liquidation or full liquidation is impossible, the termination ruling shall state that the creditor may, separately, pursuant to Article 18 of Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law, require the respondent's shareholders, directors, actual controllers, and other liquidation obligors to assume repayment liability for its debts. If a shareholder applies for compulsory liquidation and the people's court rules to terminate the compulsory liquidation procedure on the ground that liquidation or full liquidation is impossible, the termination ruling shall state that the shareholder may assert relevant rights against the controlling shareholder or other persons who actually control the company.

XV. Hearing of Derivative Litigation in Compulsory Liquidation Cases

30. Civil lawsuits concerning the company under compulsory liquidation that were initiated before the acceptance of the compulsory liquidation application and have not yet been concluded at the time of acceptance shall continue to be heard by the original court that accepted the case, but the original legal representative shall be replaced by the head of the liquidation group in accordance with the law.

31. After the people's court accepts the application for compulsory liquidation, if disputes arise over the rights and obligations of the company under compulsory liquidation, an action shall be filed with the people's court that accepted the compulsory liquidation application, and the head of the liquidation group shall represent the company in liquidation in the litigation activities. The people's court that accepted the compulsory liquidation application may, for such cases, apply the provisions of Articles 37 and 39 of the Civil Procedure Law to determine the trial court.

The above cases shall be heard by the respective trial divisions within the accepting court according to their division of functions. After the people's court accepts the application for compulsory liquidation, if disputes arise over the rights and obligations of the company under compulsory liquidation, and the parties have agreed on a valid and clear arbitration clause for the dispute, it shall be resolved by arbitration in accordance with the agreement.

XVI. Connection between Compulsory Liquidation and Bankruptcy Liquidation

32. During the compulsory liquidation of a company, if the liquidation group discovers, while clearing the company's assets and preparing the balance sheet and asset list, that the company's assets are insufficient to pay its debts, except in cases where, pursuant to Article 17 of Judicial Interpretation II of the Company Law, a debt repayment plan is formulated through negotiation with creditors and debts are repaid, the liquidation group shall, in accordance with Article 188 of the Company Law and Article 7(3) of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, apply to the people's court for a declaration of bankruptcy.

33. During the compulsory liquidation of a company, if a relevant obligee separately files a bankruptcy application with the people's court pursuant to Articles 2 and 7 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the people's court shall conduct a review in accordance with the law. If the obligee's bankruptcy application meets the requirements of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the people's court shall rule to accept it in accordance with the law. After the people's court rules to accept the bankruptcy application, it shall rule to terminate the compulsory liquidation procedure.

34. After a company's compulsory liquidation is converted into bankruptcy liquidation, if the liquidation committee in the original compulsory liquidation is composed of or joined by an intermediary institution or individual from the People's Court Intermediary Institution Manager Registry and the People's Court Individual Manager Registry, unless such intermediary institution or individual has a conflict of interest in the case or is otherwise unfit to serve as the administrator or a member of the administrator, the people's court may, in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and its judicial interpretations, appoint such intermediary institution or individual as the administrator for the bankruptcy case, or absorb such intermediary institution as a member of the newly established liquidation committee administrator.

The total compensation obtained by the above-mentioned intermediary institution or individual in the compulsory liquidation and bankruptcy liquidation of the company shall not exceed the compensation payable to the administrator or members of the administrator under the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law.

35. If the above-mentioned intermediary institution or individual is unfit to serve as the administrator or a member of the administrator in the bankruptcy liquidation, the people's court shall promptly appoint an administrator in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and relevant judicial interpretations. The original liquidation committee in the compulsory liquidation shall promptly transfer the liquidation affairs and relevant materials to the administrator. Matters that have been completed in the compulsory liquidation of the company shall be recognized as valid in the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings, provided that there is no violation of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law or relevant judicial interpretations.

VII. Conclusion of Compulsory Liquidation Proceedings

36. After the company's liquidation is completed in accordance with the law, and the liquidation committee prepares a liquidation report and submits it to the people's court for confirmation, the people's court shall rule to conclude the liquidation proceedings. After the company registration authority cancels the company's registration upon application by the liquidation committee, the company terminates.

37. Where a company's business term expires as stipulated in its articles of association, or other grounds for dissolution as stipulated in its articles of association arise, or the shareholders' meeting or general meeting resolves voluntary dissolution, and after the people's court accepts a creditor's application for compulsory liquidation but before distribution of residual assets to shareholders, the company amends its articles of association or the shareholders' meeting or general meeting resolves that the company shall continue to exist, if the applicant does not withdraw its application after both its own claims and the claims of other creditors have been fully satisfied, the people's court may, upon the request of the respondent, rule to conclude the compulsory liquidation proceedings. After the conclusion of the compulsory liquidation proceedings, the company may continue to exist.

VIII. Legal Documents in Compulsory Liquidation Cases

38. When a trial division hearing a compulsory liquidation case tries such a case, it shall issue a civil ruling for: accepting or not accepting an application for compulsory liquidation; rejecting the applicant's application; permitting or rejecting the applicant's withdrawal of the application; adopting preservation measures; confirming the liquidation plan; confirming the final liquidation report; or concluding the compulsory liquidation proceedings. It shall issue a decision for: appointing or changing members of the liquidation committee; determining the remuneration of members of the liquidation committee; extending the liquidation period; or sanctioning acts that hinder the liquidation.

For the preparation of other related legal documents, reference may be made to the styles of people's court legal documents in enterprise bankruptcy liquidation.

IX. Mutatis Mutandis Application of Bankruptcy Liquidation Procedures in Compulsory Liquidation

39. Given the similarity in specific procedural operations between compulsory liquidation and bankruptcy liquidation of companies, for circumstances not covered by the Company Law, the Second Judicial Interpretation of the Company Law, and this Meeting Summary, such as where: relevant personnel of the company under liquidation fail to properly preserve in accordance with the law the property, seals, account books, and documents under their possession and management; the liquidation committee fails to promptly take over the property, seals, account books, and documents of the company under liquidation; the company under liquidation refuses to submit to the people's court, or submits false, statements of property status, lists of debts, lists of claims, relevant financial accounting reports, and information on payment of employee wages and social insurance premiums; the company under liquidation refuses to transfer property, seals, account books, documents and other materials to the liquidation committee, or forges or destroys relevant property evidentiary materials causing the property status to be unclear; shareholders fail to fully contribute capital or withdraw capital; and directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel illegally misappropriate company property, etc., the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and its judicial interpretations may be applied mutatis mutandis.

X. Issues to Be Noted in Hearing Company Compulsory Liquidation Cases

40. Given that such cases are of a new type and involve complex legal relationships and numerous interested parties, when hearing major and difficult liquidation cases that are difficult to adjudicate, have wide-ranging implications, and implicate social stability, the people's court must, on the premise of strictly adhering to the law, firmly rely on the leadership of the Party committee and the support of the government, fully utilize various mechanisms established by local governments, and effectively carry out the work of maintaining social stability. At the same time, new situations and new problems discovered in judicial practice shall be promptly reported level by level to higher authorities. Higher people's courts shall strengthen supervision and guidance over such cases, focus on in-depth investigation and research, timely summarize trial experience, and ensure that such cases are properly adjudicated in accordance with the law.
